q: Does diesel burnt during load shedding count in a South African steel mill's CBAM figure?
title: Load shedding diesel and CBAM
short: Diesel burnt in generators to make electricity is treated as electricity, so for steel it is reported as indirect emissions and not charged today. Diesel burnt directly in process heat, mobile plant inside the site or furnaces is direct and does count. Meter the two separately.
audience: Steel mills, foundries and ferroalloy plants in South Africa running backup generators during grid outages

ul: Generator diesel: log litres and kWh produced, and report as electricity from your own plant.
Process diesel or burner oil: count as direct emissions at IPCC defaults or measured values.
Site vehicles inside the installation: follow your monitoring plan and be consistent.

p: Generator power emits more per kWh than most grids, and buyers counting Scope 3 will see it. Indirect emissions may also be extended to more goods after the Commission's review.
